destinations.name: Paris
destinations.tagline: The city of light, still glowing
destinations.description: Paris rewards slow walks: limestone facades, bakery steam, and monuments that look exactly as they do in every daydream. Come for the icons, stay for the side streets between them.
travelTips: Book museum time slots before you fly.
The Metro is faster than taxis at rush hour.
A late-night Seine walk beats another crowded viewpoint.

destinations.name: Bali
destinations.description: Bali is a study in contrast: jungle silence in Ubud, surf towns on the south coast, and ceremonies that spill into the street. It is the featured escape for a reason — the light loves a camera.
travelTips: Leave extra time — traffic across the island is real.
Dress modestly at temples; sarongs are often provided.
Sunrise at the volcano is worth the 02:00 alarm.

destinations.name: Tokyo
destinations.description: Tokyo is several cities stacked: quiet temple gardens at dawn, department-store food halls at noon, and electric nights in Shinjuku. Trains make it easy; curiosity makes it endless.
travelTips: Get a Suica or Pasmo card on day one.
Many tiny restaurants still prefer cash.
Book teamLab and popular cafés in advance.

destinations.name: Dubai
destinations.description: Dubai is spectacle done properly: towers that rewrite the skyline, a souk that still smells of spice, and a desert an hour from the mall. Go for the views, stay for the unexpected calm on the water.
travelTips: Plan outdoor sights for morning or dusk.
The Metro is inexpensive and air-conditioned.
Dress modestly in older neighbourhoods and mosques.

destinations.name: London
destinations.tagline: Parks, palaces and a thousand corners
destinations.description: London is a city of villages sewn together by the Tube. Museums are world-class and often free, parks swallow whole afternoons, and the river keeps you oriented when the streets will not.
travelTips: An Oyster or contactless card beats paper tickets.
Book the Tower and West End seats ahead.
Sunday roast is a plan, not a maybe.

destinations.name: Rome
destinations.tagline: A living museum with better pasta
destinations.description: Rome stacks centuries in a single block. You will trip over history on the way to lunch, then find a fountain that has been posing for photographs since before photography.
travelTips: Skip-the-line tickets for the Colosseum and Vatican are worth it.
Fill a bottle at the nasoni street fountains.
Dinner starts late; gelato can bridge the wait.

destinations.name: Singapore
destinations.tagline: Gardens in the sky, hawker on the street
destinations.description: Singapore is precision with soul: rainforest in a glass dome, chilli crab at a hawker centre, and a harbour that looks staged for night photographs. It is easy, delicious and compact.
travelTips: Hawker centres are the real national dish.
The MRT is spotless and obvious.
Carry a light layer for ferocious air-conditioning.

destinations.name: New York
destinations.tagline: The city that still looks like the movies
destinations.description: New York is vertical energy: brownstones, bridges, and a skyline that rearranges itself every decade. Walk more than you plan to. Eat standing up at least once.
travelTips: An unlimited MetroCard (or OMNY) pays for itself quickly.
Book The Met and Broadway before the weekend.
Sunset from a west-facing pier is free and cinematic.

destinations.name: Santorini
destinations.tagline: White walls, dark cliffs, gold hour
destinations.description: Santorini is the postcard that turns out to be real: caldera views, volcanic beaches, and villages that glow at dusk. Stay for sunrise in Oia, when the terraces belong to you.
travelTips: Oia sunset is famous for a reason — arrive early.
ATMs can be scarce in smaller villages.
A boat day on the caldera beats another cliff café.

destinations.name: Kyoto
destinations.description: Kyoto is Japan’s memory palace: torii gates in the trees, gardens raked into stillness, and neighbourhoods that still close the wooden shutters at dusk. Go early; the magic is a morning person.
travelTips: Fushimi Inari at 07:00 is a different mountain.
Reserve a tea ceremony; walk-ins fill up.
Buses are slower than they look on the map.

destinations.name: Cape Town
destinations.description: Cape Town is geography as drama: a flat-topped mountain in the middle of town, beaches that change colour with the weather, and wine country a short drive inland.
travelTips: Book Table Mountain for a clear morning, not a windy afternoon.
The Atlantic and Indian oceans really do feel different.
A designated driver is part of a Stellenbosch day.

destinations.name: Barcelona
destinations.description: Barcelona is a Mediterranean city that refused to be ordinary. Gaudí still sets the skyline, the grid of Eixample is made for wandering, and the beach is a metro ride from the Gothic Quarter.
travelTips: Sagrada Família tickets sell out — book the towers too.
Pickpockets love crowded Las Ramblas; keep bags forward.
Dinner is late; a vermouth at 19:00 is the local bridge.

places.name: Eiffel Tower
places.summary: Iron lace over the Champ de Mars.
places.description: Climb or ride to a viewing deck and watch Paris arrange itself in every direction. Go at dusk if you can — the tower sparkles on the hour.

places.name: Louvre Museum
places.summary: A palace of rooms you will not finish.
places.description: The world’s most visited museum, from Mesopotamian reliefs to the glass pyramid. Pick two wings and leave the rest for another life.

places.name: Montmartre
places.summary: Hilltop village above the city.
places.description: Sacré-Cœur, steep lanes, and a square still full of easels. Come in the morning before the portrait painters outnumber the pigeons.

places.name: Le Meurice
places.summary: Palace hotel facing the Tuileries.
places.description: Gilded salons, a Alain Ducasse dining room, and windows that look onto the gardens. A splurge that feels like a chapter of old Paris.

places.name: Hôtel des Grands Boulevards
places.summary: Playful rooms in the 2nd.
places.description: A lively, design-forward stay with a rooftop that actually gets used. Better value than the palaces, still unmistakably Paris.

places.name: Septime
places.summary: Modern French, fiercely seasonal.
places.description: A neighbourhood tasting room that still feels like the city’s most wanted table. Book the moment dates are firm.

places.name: Café de Flore
places.summary: The Left Bank, still serving coffee.
places.description: Touristy, yes — and still the right place for an omelette and a long watch over Saint-Germain.

places.name: Seine evening cruise
places.summary: Monuments from the water.
places.description: An hour on the river when the stone turns gold. Sit on the open deck; the bridges are the show.

places.name: Marais food walk
places.summary: Falafel, fromageries, hidden courtyards.
places.description: A guided graze through the Marais: market streets, a falafel counter, and the kind of cheese shop you smell before you see.

places.name: Tegalalang Rice Terraces
places.summary: Green steps carved for water and light.
places.description: Walk the ridges, drink young coconut, and photograph the terraces before midday haze. A classic for a reason.

places.name: Tanah Lot
places.summary: A temple on a rock in the surf.
places.description: Time it for late afternoon. The sea road to the shrine is closed at high tide, which is part of the theatre.

places.name: Uluwatu Temple
places.summary: Cliffside kecak at sunset.
places.description: A sea temple on a sheer headland, with monkeys who have seen every selfie. Stay for the kecak dance as the sun drops.

places.name: Hanging Gardens of Bali
places.summary: Infinity pools in the jungle canopy.
places.description: Villas strung down a valley near Ubud, with that famous split pool. Quiet, green, and unashamedly photogenic.

places.name: Potato Head Suites
places.summary: Beach club energy, Seminyak.
places.description: Design-led rooms above one of the island’s best sunset decks. Stay if you want the sea in the same sentence as dinner.

places.name: Locavore NXT
places.summary: Farm-led tasting in Ubud.
places.description: A precise, playful tasting menu built from island farms. One of Southeast Asia’s destination tables.

places.name: Canggu Beach Club
places.summary: Grilled fish, sandy feet.
places.description: A laid-back beach table for grilled catch and coconut. Come sandy; leave at golden hour.

places.name: Mount Batur sunrise trek
places.summary: A volcano before the island wakes.
places.description: A guided night climb to watch the sun rise over the caldera and, on clear days, Agung. Breakfast is boiled eggs in the steam.

places.name: Nusa Penida boat day
places.summary: Cliffs, snorkels, turquoise water.
places.description: A fast boat to Penida for Kelingking views and a snorkel over manta territory. Start early; the sea gets choppy later.

places.name: Sensō-ji
places.summary: Incense and lanterns in Asakusa.
places.description: Tokyo’s oldest temple, approached through a shopping street that has been selling snacks for centuries. Go at opening for calmer gates.

places.name: Shibuya Crossing
places.summary: The scramble, from street or sky.
places.description: Wait for the light, then walk with a thousand others. The Mag’s Park rooftop is the kinder viewpoint.

places.name: teamLab Borderless
places.summary: Rooms made of light.
places.description: An immersive digital museum that spills from one room into the next. Book a slot; wander without a map.

places.name: Park Hyatt Tokyo
places.summary: Cloud-level calm in Shinjuku.
places.description: The Lost in Translation hotel, still one of the city’s best stays: pool in the sky, New York Bar, and quiet rooms above the neon.

places.name: Onsen Ryokan Yuen Shinjuku
places.summary: A soak in the middle of the city.
places.description: Tatami rooms and a rooftop onsen a few streets from the station. Proof you do not need to leave Tokyo to slow down.

places.name: Tsukiji Outer Market
places.summary: Tamagoyaki, sushi, street steam.
places.description: The inner market moved; the outer streets still feed the city. Eat standing, then eat again.

places.name: Ichiran Shibuya
places.summary: Tonkotsu in a solo booth.
places.description: A customisable bowl in a focus booth. Touristy, efficient, and oddly meditative at 23:00.

places.name: Mount Fuji day trip
places.summary: The cone, if the clouds agree.
places.description: A coach or train day toward Kawaguchiko. Clear winter mornings are the honest bet; the mountain does not pose on command.

places.name: Ghibli Museum
places.summary: A house that thinks like a film.
places.description: Tickets are dated and sell out. No photographs inside, which is the point — you have to look.

places.name: Burj Khalifa
places.summary: The tallest anything, anywhere.
places.description: Observation decks at 124 and 148. Book sunset; the desert and the gulf both show up.

places.name: Dubai Fountain
places.summary: Water, light, the Burj as backdrop.
places.description: Free shows on the lake beside Dubai Mall. Stand on the bridge, not in the crowd at the railing.

places.name: Museum of the Future
places.summary: A calligraphy-clad oval of ideas.
places.description: Speculative exhibitions inside one of the city’s best-looking buildings. Pair with a walk along the Emirates Towers boulevard.

places.name: Burj Al Arab
places.summary: The sail, on its own island.
places.description: A suite hotel that still defines Dubai excess: gold, butlers, and a terrace over the gulf. Afternoon tea is the lighter way in.

places.name: Atlantis, The Palm
places.summary: A resort at the end of the crescent.
places.description: Aquarium suites, a waterpark, and a beach that faces the skyline. Family spectacle, done at scale.

places.name: Pierchic
places.summary: Seafood on a pier over the gulf.
places.description: A walk to a dining room surrounded by water, with the Burj Al Arab in the frame. Sunset bookings vanish first.

places.name: Al Fanar
places.summary: Emirati home cooking, courtyard style.
places.description: Machboos, luqaimat and karak in a reconstructed old Dubai courtyard. A useful counterweight to the towers.

places.name: Desert safari
places.summary: Dunes, dinner, a sky without towers.
places.description: Dune bashing, optional camel photos, and a camp dinner. Choose a small-group operator; the sunset is the point.

places.name: Dubai Marina yacht hour
places.summary: The marina skyline from the water.
places.description: A short private or shared cruise past the clustered towers. Golden hour photographs almost take themselves.

places.name: British Museum
places.summary: A free encyclopedia of objects.
places.description: Rosetta Stone to Sutton Hoo, under a great glass court. It is huge; pick a theme and ignore the rest.

places.name: Tower of London
places.summary: Crowns, ravens, a thousand years.
places.description: Yeoman Warder tours are the way in. The crown jewels queue looks worse than it is; the ravens are unionised.

places.name: Sky Garden
places.summary: A greenhouse on the 35th floor.
places.description: Free timed tickets for a public garden and bar in the Walkie Talkie. Book the day before; views run from St Paul’s to the Thames Barrier.

places.name: The Savoy
places.summary: Thames-facing Edwardian glamour.
places.description: A theatre-land palace with an American Bar that still takes mixing seriously. Afternoon tea is a production.

places.name: The Hoxton, Shoreditch
places.summary: A sociable stay east of the City.
places.description: Lively lobby, compact rooms, and a neighbourhood that rewards wandering. A mid-range favourite for a reason.

places.name: Dishoom Covent Garden
places.summary: Bombay café, London queues.
places.description: Bacon naan at breakfast, black daal at any hour. Walk in early or book; the queue is part of the folklore.

places.name: Borough Market
places.summary: A thousand lunches under iron roofs.
places.description: Cheese, bread, and a grilled sandwich you will think about later. Avoid Saturday noon if you like your elbows.

places.name: Thames clipper
places.summary: The city from the river.
places.description: An Uber Boat hop from Westminster to Greenwich. Sit outside if the weather allows; the bridges do the narration.

places.name: West End evening
places.summary: A stall seat and a late Tube.
places.description: Theatre land still delivers. Same-day TKTS in Leicester Square can be kind; otherwise book the show you actually want.

places.name: Colosseum
places.summary: The arena that still holds a crowd.
places.description: Combine with the Forum and Palatine on one ticket. Morning light on the arches is the photograph everyone wants — and should get.

places.name: Vatican Museums
places.summary: A mile of rooms, then the ceiling.
places.description: The Sistine Chapel is the destination; the map room and the pinecone courtyard are the surprises. Pre-book or suffer.

places.name: Trevi Fountain
places.summary: A coin, a wish, a thousand cameras.
places.description: Go at 07:00 or after 23:00. The marble still looks wet in the floodlights. One coin only — the rest is folklore inflation.

places.name: Hotel de Russie
places.summary: A secret garden off Piazza del Popolo.
places.description: Rocco Forte calm, a terraced garden, and a location that makes the rest of the centro a stroll.

places.name: The Beehive
places.summary: A friendly inn by Termini.
places.description: Thoughtful budget rooms, a garden café, and staff who actually like helping. Proof Rome is not only palazzi.

places.name: Roscioli
places.summary: Carbonara among the salumi.
places.description: Part deli, part dining room. Sit at the back if you can; the wine list is a second education.

places.name: Armando al Pantheon
places.summary: Trattoria in the shadow of the dome.
places.description: Roman classics without theatre. Book; the room is small and the pasta is the reason people still queue.

places.name: Twilight Trastevere walk
places.summary: Lanterns, ivy, a spritz on the piazza.
places.description: Cross Ponte Sisto as the stone warms, then lose an hour in lanes that still feel like a village. Dinner wherever the locals are standing.

places.name: Pasta-making class
places.summary: Eggs, flour, a Roman nonna energy.
places.description: A hands-on class: dough, sauce, and a lunch you actually made. Book a small group in a home kitchen, not a theatre.

places.name: Gardens by the Bay
places.summary: Supertrees and a cloud forest.
places.description: The outdoor grove is free; the cooled conservatories are the show. Stay for the night light show if the heat has not won.

places.name: Marina Bay Sands SkyPark
places.summary: The infinity edge everyone knows.
places.description: A ticketed observation deck (the pool is for guests). Go at blue hour when the bay reflects the skyline.

places.name: Chinatown
places.summary: Temples, shophouses, late satay.
places.description: Sri Mariamman, Thian Hock Keng, and Maxwell Food Centre within a few blocks. Come hungry and stay for the lanterns.

places.name: Raffles Singapore
places.summary: Whitewashed courtyards and a sling.
places.description: The restored colonial hotel, still serving the original sling in the Long Bar (peanut shells on the floor, as tradition insists).

places.name: The Warehouse Hotel
places.summary: A restored riverside godown.
places.description: Industrial bones, excellent beds, and a bar that takes tropical drinks seriously. A design stay without the atrium circus.

places.name: Hawker Chan
places.summary: Soya sauce chicken, still a pilgrimage.
places.description: The Michelin-starred stall’s descendants still serve the same glossy chicken and rice. Queue, eat, understand Singapore.

places.name: Odette
places.summary: A garden of a tasting menu.
places.description: French technique, Asian produce, a room inside the National Gallery. For a celebration night.

places.name: Night Safari
places.summary: A tram through the dark.
places.description: The world’s first nocturnal zoo. Tram first, then the walking trails when your eyes adjust.

places.name: Peranakan trail
places.summary: Tiles, kebaya, a museum of a culture.
places.description: Joo Chiat shophouses and the Peranakan Museum. Eat a laksa that actually burns.

places.name: Central Park
places.summary: The city’s green lung.
places.description: Enter at Grand Army Plaza and walk until the buildings disappear. The Mall, the lake, and a pretzel are a complete afternoon.

places.name: The Met
places.summary: Temple of Dendur and then some.
places.description: Pay-what-you-wish for New York State residents; everyone else buys a ticket. The rooftop (in season) is the secret gallery.

places.name: Brooklyn Bridge
places.summary: A walk between boroughs.
places.description: Start on the Manhattan side at sunrise or dusk. Stay on the raised pedestrian boardwalk; the photographs face south.

places.name: The Plaza
places.summary: A chateau on the park.
places.description: Gilded, storied, and still a scene. Eloise would approve of the palm court; the park is across the street.

places.name: Ace Hotel Brooklyn
places.summary: A sociable stay south of the bridge.
places.description: Industrial bones, a serious lobby bar, and a neighbourhood that has already eaten. Easier on the budget than Midtown palaces.

places.name: Katz's Delicatessen
places.summary: Pastrami that requires a strategy.
places.description: Take a ticket, know your cut, split a sandwich. The line is the tax; the meat is the refund.

places.name: Le Bernardin
places.summary: Seafood, almost silent.
places.description: One of the city’s great dining rooms. Jackets, tasting menus, and fish treated with religious attention.

places.name: Broadway evening
places.summary: A marquee, an orchestra, a late diner.
places.description: TKTS or a lottery can work; otherwise buy the seat you want. Walk Times Square afterwards only if you enjoy chaos.

places.name: Staten Island Ferry sunset
places.summary: The harbour, the statue, no ticket.
places.description: A free round trip with the skyline as the show. Stand on the right side outbound for the statue.

places.name: Oia sunset
places.summary: Blue domes, a thousand cameras, gold light.
places.description: Walk the caldera path from Fira if you have the legs, or arrive early and claim a wall. The sun is punctual; the crowd is not.

places.name: Fira
places.summary: The island’s lively rim.
places.description: Cafés, the cable car, and a caldera view that does not require a hotel key. The Orthodox cathedral steps are a quiet pause.

places.name: Red Beach
places.summary: Volcanic sand under rust cliffs.
places.description: A short walk from Akrotiri. Bring water shoes; the colour is the point, not the loungers.

places.name: Canaves Oia
places.summary: Cave suites on the caldera.
places.description: Whitewashed luxury with private terraces over the water. The kind of stay people get engaged at.

places.name: Vedema Resort
places.summary: A wine-country hide in Megalochori.
places.description: Quieter than Oia, with a cellar and a village that still has a bakery. A luxury stay that sleeps.

places.name: Ammoudi Fish Tavern
places.summary: Grilled catch at the waterline.
places.description: Descend the steps from Oia (or take a taxi back up). Order whatever came in that morning.

places.name: Seaside Santo
places.summary: A long lunch on Perivolos.
places.description: Beachfront, unhurried, and close enough to the water to hear it. The Greek salad is not ironic.

places.name: Caldera sail
places.summary: Volcanic islands and a swim stop.
places.description: A catamaran afternoon: hot springs, the red and white beaches from the water, and a sunset you do not have to share with a wall.

places.name: Santorini wine tour
places.summary: Assyrtiko in a volcanic cellar.
places.description: Three houses, a driver, and a grape that tastes like stone and sea. Santo and Venetsanos are the usual pillars.

places.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
places.summary: A thousand vermilion gates.
places.description: Start at dawn and you may have a stretch of tunnel to yourself. The summit is optional; the first 15 minutes are the photograph.

places.name: Arashiyama bamboo grove
places.summary: Green light, a path like a film still.
places.description: Walk through early, then continue to the river and Tenryu-ji. Midday is a shuffle; dawn is a gift.

places.name: Kinkaku-ji
places.summary: The gold pavilion on the pond.
places.description: You will not go inside; you will circle the water and understand why every postcard chose this angle.

places.name: Hiiragiya Ryokan
places.summary: A classic inn near the river.
places.description: Tatami, kaiseki in-room, and a wooden architecture that has hosted writers for a century. Book far ahead.

places.name: Ace Hotel Kyoto
places.summary: A contemporary stay in a former telephone building.
places.description: Kengo Kuma interiors, a lively lobby, and a location that makes Gion a night walk. Modern Kyoto without the onsen ritual.

places.name: Nishiki Market
places.summary: Pickled everything, still-warm tofu.
places.description: A narrow food street for grazing. Do not try to have a sit-down meal in the lane; snack, then sit elsewhere.

places.name: Kikunoi
places.summary: Kaiseki as a season on a tray.
places.description: A three-star house in Higashiyama. Reserve as soon as you have dates; this is the meal people rearrange flights for.

places.name: Tea ceremony
places.summary: Matcha, tatami, a practised quiet.
places.description: A small-group ceremony with explanation. Camellia or a temple-affiliated tea house; leave the rushing at the door.

places.name: Gion evening walk
places.summary: Lanterns on Hanami-koji.
places.description: A dusk walk through Gion. Be courteous if you see a geiko — this is a neighbourhood, not a set.

places.name: Table Mountain
places.summary: A flat summit above the city.
places.description: Cable car if the wind allows; hike Platteklip if you have legs and a clear morning. The view is the Cape Peninsula in one turn.

places.name: Cape of Good Hope
places.summary: Where two oceans argue.
places.description: A day on the peninsula: Chapman’s Peak, the Cape, and a lighthouse if the legs still work. Baboons have seen your sandwiches.

places.name: Bo-Kaap
places.summary: Colour-blocked houses, a spice history.
places.description: Walk, do not just photograph. The museum and a Cape Malay cooking class add the part the facades cannot tell.

places.name: Belmond Mount Nelson
places.summary: Pink walls and a famous tea.
places.description: A colonial grande dame at the foot of the mountain, with gardens that make a city stay feel like a retreat.

places.name: The Silo
places.summary: A grain elevator turned jewel box.
places.description: Rooms above the Zeitz Museum, with pillowed windows over the harbour. Design hotel of the decade, still.

places.name: The Test Kitchen
places.summary: A tasting menu that put the city on lists.
places.description: Bookings are a sport. If you miss it, the city’s wider dining scene is no consolation prize — it is the main event.

places.name: Kloof Street House
places.summary: A garden villa of a dining room.
places.description: Candlelit, leafy, and reliably good. A neighbourhood table that works for a first night in town.

places.name: Boulders Beach penguins
places.summary: African penguins, close enough to hear.
places.description: A boardwalk colony in Simon’s Town. Morning is calmer; do not step off the path — they nest in the scrub.

places.name: Stellenbosch wine day
places.summary: Oaks, estate lawns, a designated driver.
places.description: Three estates and a long lunch. The mountains do as much work as the wine. Book a driver; the N1 is not a tasting note.

places.name: Sagrada Família
places.summary: A forest of stone, still unfinished.
places.description: Book a tower. The interior is the revelation — stained glass that behaves like weather. Gaudí is not a punchline here.

places.name: Park Güell
places.summary: Mosaic benches and a view of the sea.
places.description: Timed entry for the monumental zone. The rest of the park is free and almost as photogenic.

places.name: Gothic Quarter
places.summary: A maze that predates the grid.
places.description: Lose the map between the cathedral and Plaça Reial. The quarter is at its best just after breakfast, before the tour groups.

places.name: Hotel Casa Fuster
places.summary: Modernista palace on Passeig de Gràcia.
places.description: A landmark building with a rooftop that looks down the avenue. Piano in the café, city at the door.

places.name: Cotton House Hotel
places.summary: A former cotton guild, still dressed up.
places.description: Tapestries, a spiral stair, and a pool in the Eixample. A luxury stay that feels like a private club.
places.location: Gran Via de les Corts Catalanes

places.name: Tickets
places.summary: Playful tapas, if it is still in season.
places.description: Adrià-world theatre on a plate. Bookings are scarce; a well-chosen tapas crawl is the honest backup.

places.name: La Boqueria
places.summary: Fruit cones and a counter lunch.
places.description: Enter from the back streets, not Las Ramblas. Eat at a stall counter; the fruit juice is a tourist tax you may still pay.

places.name: Beach bike to Barceloneta
places.summary: A flat ride from Gothic to the sea.
places.description: Rent a bike and follow the waterfront. Swim if the flags agree; vermouth after if they do not.

places.name: Montserrat day trip
places.summary: A serrated mountain and a monastery.
places.description: Train plus rack railway. Hike a peak if the cloud is kind; the boys’ choir sings at noon on many days.
